# Sai Urja Indo Ventures Limited

SME research under Master Prompt v3.0 · Information cutoff: 20 October 2026 · Market reference: 19 October 2026 · INR crore unless stated

## 1. Executive Verdict

Sai Urja is a labour-intensive operation-and-maintenance contractor serving mainly thermal power plants. Recurring maintenance needs, repeat customers and substantial reported sales growth are real strengths. They do not yet establish a durable compounder: one customer represents 74.77% of FY26 sales, working capital extends far beyond billed debtors, and the original accounts disclose historical missing edit trails and unquantified fund movements classified as trade payables without supporting supply transactions. The IPO provides meaningful new capital, but a proposed ₹6.6 crore debt repayment is not evidence that it occurred. At the secondary-source 19 October close of ₹221.90, current-share earnings multiples are demanding, and conditional financing/valuation experiments cannot substitute for verified cash and liabilities. Classification: **Hold — unresolved**, with BQS, GQS and IAS unscoreable. This is a concentrated services-growth/possible special-situation research thesis, not an evidence-backed compounder. Independent closure of the accounting issues, post-IPO bank/debt reconciliation and evidence of cash-backed service growth would matter more than a lower quotation alone. [E01–E15]

## 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence

Legal issuer: Sai Urja Indo Ventures Limited, formerly Sai Urja Indo Ventures Private Limited; incorporated 17 May 2012 and converted to public status on 6 February 2025. ISIN INE1LLG01019; BSE code 544958, security ID SAIURJA. Listing began 5 October 2026. This is the original universe's abbreviated “Sai Urja Indo,” not another similarly named energy company. The economic rubric is labour-intensive O&M/industrial support, although the supplied universe classified it as civil construction. [E12; RHP cover, pp88,221]

The historical default is consolidated Ind AS as restated in the IPO documents, including equity-accounted interests in two partnerships. No subsidiary is consolidated line-by-line and there is no NCI deduction. Aspire Associates moved from 33.33% to 50% after its 19 August 2025 reconstitution; Shikhar Associates is 40% owned. Neither firm's full sales or payroll is added to Sai Urja revenue. The accounts' equity-method description conflicts with a later FVTPL policy paragraph; actual reported carrying values and separate associate earnings are preserved, not rewritten. [E01; RHP pp260,269,276]

Original FY21–23 statutory standalone statements provide longer context, not a seamless earnings/cash-flow series. Their P&L tax, reserves, cash classifications and later restatements require explicit bridges. FY24 is a special-purpose Ind AS restatement over statutory AS; FY25/26 use Ind AS. Do not infer an accounting framework from SME status or an old audit template. [E01–E03]

The five-year investment horizon runs from 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031; ten years is an additional feasibility test. The equity hurdle is an analyst-assumed 15% nominal INR annual return before personal taxes, with 12% and 18% sensitivity. WACC is separately assumed at 14–18%, reflecting small-company concentration and financing risk, not set equal to the equity hurdle. The ₹5 lakh liquidity reference is illustrative, not a suitable allocation recommendation. All prices are historical and no order is proposed. Sources were retrieved later, but no post-cutoff operating outcome is used as if known on 20 October. [E14–E15]

### GOV: 4 · Medium

FY24 audit-trail control was ineffective and FY25 original notes explicitly say audit trail was not maintained. Original FY21–23 CARO excluded PF/ESI from the no-long-overdue-dues statement. The RHP retains a disclosure that certain party balances recorded as trade payables represent cash receipts/payments without underlying purchases/sales or detailed supporting records; the affected amount is unknown.

Counterevidence: Main audit and IFC opinions are unmodified. Old IGST arrears were paid 26 August 2025; promoter property advance 0.4999 cr was recovered in FY25 and gross promoter loan flows were repaid. No substantiated fraud or lender-default finding was located.

Judgment: Repeated control/recordkeeping and statutory-compliance weaknesses merit 4, but severe abuse or intentional diversion is not established. G1 is a documentary hold, not a governance-fail override. [E03, E04, E05, E06] No historical factor above 8: relevant restated history is four years or confidence is Medium; older AS history is qualified rather than discarded.

### MOAT: 4 · Medium

O&M qualifications, repeat PSU work and performance history create useful tender access, but one customer supplies 74.77% of FY26 revenue and payroll absorbs 87.31% of sales. Contracts are contestable and no independent market share or pricing-power series was established.

Counterevidence: Repeat work is tangible: issuer reports 99.65% repeat revenue in FY26, and execution across multiple plants/states takes field organization and compliance skill. A larger Power Mech O&M business and technical peers show the sector is not uniformly undifferentiated.

Judgment: Operational competence is not a demonstrated durable barrier. Narrow margins, manpower substitution and tender concentration leave economics vulnerable to a single procurement decision. [E09, E10, E13] No historical factor above 8: relevant restated history is four years or confidence is Medium; older AS history is qualified rather than discarded.

### REV: NS · Low for underlying economic growth; High for disclosed-sales arithmetic

The older DRHP supplies a restated FY23 revenue 28.3935 cr; with FY24–26 of 45.6164/65.5242/85.1097 cr, the three-interval reported CAGR is 44.185%. No subsidiary acquisition revenue is consolidated line-by-line.

Counterevidence: FY26 projects and serviced plants are unchanged at 36 and 15, while reported personnel count falls 2469 to 2058; RHP p195 defines during-year deployment while p199 uses a March 31 narrative. Payroll-spread proxy grows 20.73% in FY26 and 17.47% CAGR over FY24–26, far slower than gross sales. Person-days, tariff escalation and scope/mix are not quantified.

Judgment: The gross service-sales schedule starts at 9, limited-history cap 8, but that is diagnostic only. Wage pass-through and materially different gross-versus-retained economics are not bounded well enough to assign underlying revenue expansion. Retain NS rather than pretend all nominal scaling is organic volume. [E01, E02, E09, E11] No historical factor above 8: relevant restated history is four years or confidence is Medium; older AS history is qualified rather than discarded.

### DUR: 5 · Medium

Coal-fired installed assets require continuing O&M; the issuer has a real 97.0184 cr unexecuted balance at 15 June 2026 across ongoing/not-started contracts. Licenses and established client access create an addressable, finite runway.

Counterevidence: The 159.6704 cr headline includes 62.652 cr already invoiced; no current cutoff backlog reconciliation or binding five-year path was located. Demand access is concentrated and tender re-awards can be lost. A secondary-supported 18 October INR 12.98 crore NTECL L1 bid is a positive pipeline update, but firm award and timing remain unverified and it is excluded from executable backlog.

Judgment: Adequate demand durability is balanced against renewal, concentration and working-capital constraints. The model cannot turn installed power capacity into guaranteed accessible orders. [E09, E10, E11] No historical factor above 8: relevant restated history is four years or confidence is Medium; older AS history is qualified rather than discarded.

### CAP: NS · Low

The diagnostic productive-capital calculation includes unbilled claims, retention, pledged deposits and all operating commitments, not only small PPE. Reported post-tax EBIT and rising sales produce superficially attractive return ratios.

Counterevidence: RHP note 50 discloses that certain party balances recorded as trade payables represent cash receipts/payments without underlying purchases/sales or detailed supporting records. Their amount is unknown, and their operating-versus-financing classification is unresolved. Security-deposit recoverability and noncash accretion/amortization complicate the denominator and cash investment bridge. No project/cohort cash return is disclosed.

Judgment: Present exact asset/funding and incremental-capital diagnostics but no reliable sustainable incremental ROIC score. A low fixed-asset base does not prove capital-light economics. [E02, E05, E07, E08] No historical factor above 8: relevant restated history is four years or confidence is Medium; older AS history is qualified rather than discarded.

### CASH: 3 · Medium

FY24–26 reported CFO totals 0.3020 cr against 8.7450 cr group PAT, a 3.45% ratio of sums. CFO is negative in both FY25 and FY26; retentions/security deposits and the wage-liability unwind absorb funds.

Counterevidence: FY24 CFO 3.3509 cr was positive; latest billed receivables declined and IPO capital can fund timing gaps. Reported cash-flow classification has limitations, but plausible corrections do not establish robust customer cash realization.

Judgment: Recurring weak realization, not capex, supports 3. Apply the disclosed GQS≤5 override while retaining NS for missing growth/capital factors; this does not diagnose an actual default. [E02, E07, E08] No historical factor above 8: relevant restated history is four years or confidence is Medium; older AS history is qualified rather than discarded.

Counterevidence: Fresh-issue gross 20.66544 cr is meaningful; lenders existed and no lender default was reported. The June debt update and restricted IPO objects are evidence against assuming the issuer has no financing options.

Judgment: Cutoff free cash, actual proceeds deployment, drawing-power availability and maturity conflicts are unresolved. Model shortfalls are conditional experiments, not proof the issuer failed G3. [E02, E08, E12, E14] No historical factor above 8: relevant restated history is four years or confidence is Medium; older AS history is qualified rather than discarded.

Revenue and number of projects scaled strongly before FY26, with repeat execution and entry into additional states. The issuer completed the IPO and had an identifiable order base.

Counterevidence: FY26 project count/plant count are flat; concentration in one customer increases, and deductions and recoveries rise to 0.1294 cr. Prospectus quantity/percentage/classification inconsistencies reduce confidence in performance communication.

Judgment: Mixed observable delivery merits 5. There is no invented promise that management never made; post-IPO use-of-proceeds delivery is too recent to judge. [E09, E10, E11, E12] No historical factor above 8: relevant restated history is four years or confidence is Medium; older AS history is qualified rather than discarded.

Judgment: Adequate recurring profit progress with meaningful normalization and per-share caveats. Cash weakness is assessed in CASH, not used as a duplicate arbitrary deduction here. [E01, E02, E07, E12] No historical factor above 8: relevant restated history is four years or confidence is Medium; older AS history is qualified rather than discarded.

Counterevidence: Optimistic financed operating paths may support returns, but no supported actual entry balance or approved future capital is established.

[E14] No historical factor above 8: relevant restated history is four years or confidence is Medium; older AS history is qualified rather than discarded.

The dominant-customer loss/delay path simultaneously cuts revenue, pressures payroll margin and traps unbilled/security claims. Intraperiod and terminal-reserve failures suppress all ordinary shareholder returns.

Counterevidence: New IPO capital and continuing plant operations provide possible buffers; customer public-sector identity does not mean all claims are lost. No quantified liquidation-recovery waterfall is established.

Judgment: Permanent-loss risk is high qualitatively; current shareholder recoveries and credible stress-funding availability are insufficiently evidenced for a numeric factor. [E08, E09, E14] No historical factor above 8: relevant restated history is four years or confidence is Medium; older AS history is qualified rather than discarded.

Judgment: Price-implied growth/margins remain assumption-dependent on unverified cash and capital classifications. Retain all trial outcomes without forcing a price-expectations score. [E12, E14, E15] No historical factor above 8: relevant restated history is four years or confidence is Medium; older AS history is qualified rather than discarded.

Listed 5 October 2026, only 11 possible sessions exist through 19 October; 20/60-session histories cannot exist. The 1200-share market lot is supported by a qualified reproduction of the listing notice, making the ₹5 lakh reference position granular.

## 4. Business Overview

The company maintains electrical, control-and-instrumentation and mechanical systems; operates boiler/turbine/generator, coal-handling and merry-go-round infrastructure; and supplies housekeeping, overhaul and manpower services. Its customer purchases availability, safe staffing, maintenance execution and compliance rather than a proprietary manufactured product. The supplier must recruit and deploy people, fund wages/statutory benefits, provide tender/performance security, execute work and obtain customer certification before invoices and collections. [E09; RHP pp190–219,307–309]

Contracts include annual maintenance engagements commonly lasting one to three years, performance-linked work, manpower supply and short-term bill-of-quantity tasks. The issuer describes a monthly billing process with administrative verification before accounts clearance and approximately 50–60 days for realization. Meanwhile wages are generally due in the first week and statutory payments in the next month. Even a profitable contract can therefore need cash before the customer pays. RHP's historical debtor-day average does not include every retention or security deposit, so it understates the full capital tied to winning and servicing a contract. [E08–E09; RHP pp120–124]

Reported operations cover 21 locations in nine states over the recent three-year window, with electrical licenses in five states at the RHP date. The reported 2,058 personnel is not an annual person-day measure. RHP p195 defines deployed manpower during the year, whereas p199 describes the same figure as at 31 March 2026; neither average annual staffing nor billed hours is established. Another narrative uses 1,969 personnel at a different reporting date. No reconciliation of these definitions or dates is invented. Public-sector revenue is 92.27% in FY26. Government-related customers can reduce some counterparty credit risk while increasing administrative, certification and payment-timing risk. A famous plant or customer is not an endorsement of the security. [E09]

## 5. Moat / Industry Position

Proposed mechanism: tender prequalification, field experience, licenses and local labour organization allow participation in repeat maintenance work. Evidence: repeated contracts and operations across several large power stations. Durability: established staffing, safety routines and proven execution take time to replicate. Failure mode: a capable competing contractor can recruit similar personnel, meet qualification requirements and underbid; a customer can rebid or reduce scope. The record does not quantify switching costs, sustained pricing power or a defined market-share denominator. [E09–E10]

Concentration has worsened: the largest customer's share rises from 49.99% in FY24 to 74.77% in FY26. Losing one award, delayed certification or an unrecovered wage increase can overwhelm the benefit from many smaller client logos. Repeat business supports operational credibility, but concentration and repeated public tenders make it a mixed rather than strong moat. The document's repeat-revenue table is not internally additive: its FY26 repeat amount plus new-customer revenue exceeds total revenue. The narrative 99.65% figure is attributed to management, not treated as a precisely reconciled audited KPI. [E09–E11]

Reported expansion is not automatically real volume. Neither acquired subsidiaries nor currency translation explains the sales increase: the issuer has no line-by-line subsidiaries and transactions are described as INR-only. However, service scope, tariff recovery, minimum-wage escalation, person-days and contract mix are not separately quantified. FY26 reports the same 15 plants and 36 projects as FY25, with a lower reported personnel count. That does not prove shrinking activity: the document mixes during-year and March 31 descriptions, and neither is a measure of annual person-days supplied. It does mean gross sales alone cannot establish volume growth. [E09–E11]

A useful economic cross-check is revenue less employee expense, explicitly **not gross profit** because it still excludes consumables and other delivery costs. It grows more slowly than gross sales in the recent window. The still narrower revenue less payroll and materials is ₹1.5000/5.9583/7.1949/8.5221 crore in FY23/24/25/26; its FY24–26 CAGR is 19.595%. This is another service residual, not an accounting gross-margin reconstruction. The exceptionally thin FY23 residual is a distorted earnings base, so the larger three-year percentage cannot be treated as stable repeatable economics. #### Scope and reproducibility

model.py uses only the Python standard library and reads only adjacent model_inputs.json unless an input mapping is supplied. It never reads a source PDF, network endpoint, another issuer's files or a third-party package. API: run(M, label, scenario, years, overrides=None, **changes); build_models(M=None, destination=None). Monetary arithmetic uses Decimal with 60-digit intermediate precision and 1e-18-crore ledger rounding. Shares are integers. Monetary outputs are lossless strings. JSON serialization is canonical and gzip timestamps are zero; all 687 full paths, including failures, are retained. The independent verify_model.py does not import the engine or trust self-certified reconciliation flags. It independently reconstructs the current and noncurrent gratuity schedules and rejects both missing-payment and duplicate-payment mutations.

These are conditional experiments, not forecasts or a reconstruction of actual cash balances. The 31 March 2026 opening precedes the 19 October 2026 secondary-market entry. Seven explicitly unobserved bridge periods and exactly 60 or 120 post-entry monthly periods are retained. Actual June borrowing differs from March; the model does not claim that later bank balances, proceeds deployment or drawing power are known. A hypothetical funding failure is not an actual default. No supported base IRR follows from a merely hypothetical financing rescue.

Opening reported cash 0.3475 includes bank 0.0068 and physical cash 0.3407; a bank-balance-only sensitivity is separate. No unused sanction becomes cash automatically. Gross AR 10.515 includes 0.3713 doubtful, older-than-two-year balances without an allowance. Other working-capital stocks are inventory, other operating financial assets, contract deposits/EMD/retentions, payables and customer advances; ratios move linearly from opening to target over the first year while revenue compounds by actual days/365. All positive working-capital changes are funded at period start and releases arrive only at the ending 19th.

Contract deposits, EMD and retentions 9.1135 plus pledged FD 0.4502 are not free cash. Their full amounts enter productive capital. Other current financial assets 1.0326 include prepaid expenses and unquantified prepaid IPO costs and are not independently monetized. No refund of the income-tax asset 0.2209 is assumed. Listed investments 0.1636 and equity-accounted associate investment 0.2075 are nonoperating, added separately at book value only when the survival tests permit valuation. #### Claims and event ordering

Opening statutory claims 2.0242 and other cash claims 1.1203 (including audit fee) settle over 12 assumed installments. They are not included again in recurring trade payables. Opening gratuity 0.8334 comprises current 0.7376 and noncurrent 0.0958. The current portion is settled across the first 12 assumed monthly start installments; the noncurrent portion is settled across the subsequent 48. Each installment is bounded by its remaining component, with the final installment settling rounding residue. Every payment reduces free cash and the aggregate liability once, so only the remaining provision reduces productive invested capital. The separately labeled full-payment stress on 19 March 2027 accelerates only the then-remaining provision, allocating payment to current before noncurrent and never repaying an amount already settled. No opening gratuity remains at the 5- or 10-year terminal dates. These are conservative analyst timing assumptions, not assertions about actual due dates, payments or default. Future payroll cash costs remain in the operating-cost assumptions; no new unpaid gratuity provision or additional cash tax benefit is created. The prior FY25 IGST 7.31 lakh was settled on 26 August 2025, before the opening, and is never paid twice. There is no opening income-tax liability; the net tax asset is not cash. Each period processes dated financing/IPO events at the starting boundary (April 1 for the first period after the March 31 closing balance), then opening claims, scheduled opening-gratuity installments, scheduled principal, positive working-capital investment and capex. A specified portion of cash operating costs is paid seven days later, before collections. Named events between boundaries occur on their exact dates, never accelerated. Cash interest is the integral of outstanding debt times its applicable annual rate times exact days/365 between principal events; it is paid at the ending boundary before collections. The first day between the March 31 closing balance and April 1 payments accrues on opening debt, then dated principal changes determine subsequent daily interest. Ending collections equal revenue less the remaining operating costs. Negative working-capital release then arrives. Taxes accrue at the disclosed 25.168% section 115BAA rate on positive EBIT less actual modeled cash interest, without a loss-tax cash benefit; accumulated tax is paid at ending 19ths in March, June, September and December. #### Survival, reinvestment and valuation

Every event records exact pool changes, claim changes, free-cash change and date/share state; running free cash and all restricted/claim balances are losslessly reconstructed from opening. Monthly opening/closing pool and claim checkpoints, cash minima and the first breach provide independent cross-checks. Each full event is stored once globally and monthly rows carry its exact sequence references. Every event updates free cash, all restricted pools and every claim exactly. Restricted pools and claims may never become negative. Any free-cash value below zero permanently blocks all ordinary terminal EV, shareholder value, IRR/CAGR, hurdle price and normalized P/E return. The negative number is a hypothetical unfunded diagnostic balance, not an overdraft. Later proceeds cannot cure an earlier missed obligation. All subsequent diagnostic events and every failed trial remain visible.

A cash-surviving path must also cover its terminal reserve: one next-year operating month plus all unpaid income taxes, one month cash interest and next 12-month principal. A renewed OD is entirely reserved as a next-year maturity, not forgiven or indefinitely refinanced. Reserve failure suppresses ordinary returns. Every WACC/g sensitivity cell independently recomputes its reserve and sustainability gate.

Productive invested capital = closing ONWC net of any remaining opening gratuity + PPE/ROU/intangibles + capital advance + pledged deposits. ONWC includes the full contract deposits/EMD/retentions and permanently uncollected doubtful invoices. Neither operating cash nor nonoperating investments are in this denominator. Earned ROIC = min(scenario target, positive normalized NOPAT / actual modeled productive IC). Next-year NOPAT grows by g; productive reinvestment = next-year NOPAT × g / earned ROIC. Required operating cash also grows from one current month of cash operating costs to one next-year month; its positive increase is additionally deducted because operating cash is excluded from productive IC. Terminal FCFF = next-year NOPAT − productive reinvestment − operating cash growth. Positive NOPAT, ROIC > g, WACC > g and positive FCFF are all required.

Operating EV = FCFF / (WACC − g). Ordinary equity = EV + cash above operating/tax/interest reserves + separate nonoperating investments − all financial debt/leases − unpaid legacy non-tax claims, floored at zero. The full principal-inclusive reserve remains a funding gate, not a second subtraction of debt principal. Unspent IPO cash and pledged FD are not added as distributable cash. No free-cash subtotal is discounted and also counted in terminal retained cash. No post-entry dividends are assumed. Shareholder terminal price uses the actual terminal integer share count, including future dilution; CAGR uses exactly 5 or 10 entry-to-exit anniversary years.

Normalized P/E cross-checks use next-year parent EBIT less financing interest and tax, then add excess cash and separate nonoperating investments. Debt is not subtracted again from P/E equity value. The 10/15/20 multiples are transparent illustrative checks, not verified peer fair values or a substitute for the operating EV model. All P/E outputs obey the same survival gates.

Core bear/base/bull cases span both 5/10-year horizons and unfinanced, future-funded and early 5 funded policies. Operating two-way sensitivity is 4 growth rates × 4 margins × 2 horizons. Each full path contains 3 WACCs × 3 terminal-growth cells. Reverse growth tests 0–100% inclusive in 5-percentage-point increments for both horizons and all three financing policies, retaining all failures and reporting sampled growth satisfying 1×/5×/10× and 12%/15%/18% hurdles. Entry-price re-solving runs all three operating scenarios and both horizons at every price ₹1, 6, ..., 401. ## 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path

The strongest bear case is a loss or delayed renewal of the largest customer, or slower certification of its unbilled work. Revenue falls while labour, statutory payments and site costs cannot instantly adjust. Margins compress; security deposits and retention are released late; a performance guarantee or labour claim consumes more cash. Borrowing access then depends on drawing power, collateral, timely compliance and lenders. Rescue equity, if available, may dilute current holders at an unfavorable price. This is a linked business/cash/financing path, not a standalone P/E derating. [E04–E10,E14]

The single thesis-break variable is **cash-backed validity and collection of recognized service claims after wages, statutory dues and contract-security funding**. Rising accounting sales are not enough. Evidence that the disputed classification is merely ordinary, fully documented financing and that earned claims collect would materially improve the thesis. Conversely, substantiated material uncollectible revenue or abusive fund use is more serious than a temporary share-price decline. [E05,E08]

Permanent-loss risk is assessed qualitatively as High, with confidence constrained by the missing liability/recovery detail. This does not mean a default has occurred or is forecast with a stated probability. Main audits are unmodified, old IGST was settled, promoter loans were repaid, IPO cash was raised and real work continues. Those are the strongest counterarguments to an overly severe reading. They do not independently close accounting support or establish funded growth. No exact liquidation recovery is asserted. [E03–E06,E12]

The market may already price growth and the new IPO float; no claim of informational uniqueness is made. What differentiates this analysis is the separation of gross contract value from unexecuted work, operating cash from accounting profit, legal capital issuance from hypothetical finance and observed financial concerns from unsupported accusations.

## 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility

A fivefold share-price return needs about 37.97% annual growth over five years or 17.46% over ten; tenfold requires about 58.49% or 25.89%. Business sales growth, enterprise-value growth and per-share return are not interchangeable. With positive consistent earnings, price multiple equals revenue multiple × net-margin ratio × initial/final diluted shares × terminal/entry P/E. In this issuer, new-share funding and working-capital needs must be solved with that identity, not added afterward. [E14]

Secondary market/notice records are labelled secondary-supported, not primary-verified V; their arithmetic may be C without upgrading source quality. Attributed management KPIs remain M.

Open questions with decision impact:

1. What exact amounts/counterparties and transactions comprise the unsupported trade-payable balances, and how do correct classifications change CFO and IC?
2. Was the audit trail operated and preserved throughout FY26 and after IPO, and what independent evidence closes the earlier failure?
3. What were bank cash, pledged/restricted balances, actual IPO debt repayments and usable drawing-power limits on 19–20 October?
4. Which unbilled claims have been certified, invoiced and collected? What losses or delays are embedded in doubtful balances, retention and undated security deposits?

The exact model specification and all trials are retained, including failed cases. The authored-input aggregate fingerprint is **not** the SHA256 of report.md or company_record.json; verification.json separately binds those exact file paths and byte hashes. sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.content_markdown: Sai Urja is a labour-intensive operation-and-maintenance contractor serving mainly thermal power plants. Recurring maintenance needs, repeat customers and substantial reported sales growth are real strengths. They do not yet establish a durable compounder: one customer represents 74.77% of FY26 sales, working capital extends far beyond billed debtors, and the original accounts disclose historical missing edit trails and unquantified fund movements classified as trade payables without supporting supply transactions. The IPO provides meaningful new capital, but a proposed ₹6.6 crore debt repayment is not evidence that it occurred. At the secondary-source 19 October close of ₹221.90, current-share earnings multiples are demanding, and conditional financing/valuation experiments cannot substitute for verified cash and liabilities. Classification: **Hold — unresolved**, with BQS, GQS and IAS unscoreable. This is a concentrated services-growth/possible special-situation research thesis, not an evidence-backed compounder. Independent closure of the accounting issues, post-IPO bank/debt reconciliation and evidence of cash-backed service growth would matter more than a lower quotation alone. [E01–E15]

### GOV: 4 · Medium

FY24 audit-trail control was ineffective and FY25 original notes explicitly say audit trail was not maintained. Original FY21–23 CARO excluded PF/ESI from the no-long-overdue-dues statement. The RHP retains a disclosure that certain party balances recorded as trade payables represent cash receipts/payments without underlying purchases/sales or detailed supporting records; the affected amount is unknown.

Counterevidence: Main audit and IFC opinions are unmodified. Old IGST arrears were paid 26 August 2025; promoter property advance 0.4999 cr was recovered in FY25 and gross promoter loan flows were repaid. No substantiated fraud or lender-default finding was located.

Judgment: Repeated control/recordkeeping and statutory-compliance weaknesses merit 4, but severe abuse or intentional diversion is not established. G1 is a documentary hold, not a governance-fail override. [E03, E04, E05, E06] No historical factor above 8: relevant restated history is four years or confidence is Medium; older AS history is qualified rather than discarded.

### MOAT: 4 · Medium

O&M qualifications, repeat PSU work and performance history create useful tender access, but one customer supplies 74.77% of FY26 revenue and payroll absorbs 87.31% of sales. Contracts are contestable and no independent market share or pricing-power series was established.

Counterevidence: Repeat work is tangible: issuer reports 99.65% repeat revenue in FY26, and execution across multiple plants/states takes field organization and compliance skill. A larger Power Mech O&M business and technical peers show the sector is not uniformly undifferentiated.

Judgment: Operational competence is not a demonstrated durable barrier. Narrow margins, manpower substitution and tender concentration leave economics vulnerable to a single procurement decision. [E09, E10, E13] No historical factor above 8: relevant restated history is four years or confidence is Medium; older AS history is qualified rather than discarded.

### REV: NS · Low for underlying economic growth; High for disclosed-sales arithmetic

The older DRHP supplies a restated FY23 revenue 28.3935 cr; with FY24–26 of 45.6164/65.5242/85.1097 cr, the three-interval reported CAGR is 44.185%. No subsidiary acquisition revenue is consolidated line-by-line.

Counterevidence: FY26 projects and serviced plants are unchanged at 36 and 15, while reported personnel count falls 2469 to 2058; RHP p195 defines during-year deployment while p199 uses a March 31 narrative. Payroll-spread proxy grows 20.73% in FY26 and 17.47% CAGR over FY24–26, far slower than gross sales. Person-days, tariff escalation and scope/mix are not quantified.

Judgment: The gross service-sales schedule starts at 9, limited-history cap 8, but that is diagnostic only. Wage pass-through and materially different gross-versus-retained economics are not bounded well enough to assign underlying revenue expansion. Retain NS rather than pretend all nominal scaling is organic volume. [E01, E02, E09, E11] No historical factor above 8: relevant restated history is four years or confidence is Medium; older AS history is qualified rather than discarded.

### DUR: 5 · Medium

Coal-fired installed assets require continuing O&M; the issuer has a real 97.0184 cr unexecuted balance at 15 June 2026 across ongoing/not-started contracts. Licenses and established client access create an addressable, finite runway.

Counterevidence: The 159.6704 cr headline includes 62.652 cr already invoiced; no current cutoff backlog reconciliation or binding five-year path was located. Demand access is concentrated and tender re-awards can be lost. A secondary-supported 18 October INR 12.98 crore NTECL L1 bid is a positive pipeline update, but firm award and timing remain unverified and it is excluded from executable backlog.

Judgment: Adequate demand durability is balanced against renewal, concentration and working-capital constraints. The model cannot turn installed power capacity into guaranteed accessible orders. [E09, E10, E11] No historical factor above 8: relevant restated history is four years or confidence is Medium; older AS history is qualified rather than discarded.

### CAP: NS · Low

The diagnostic productive-capital calculation includes unbilled claims, retention, pledged deposits and all operating commitments, not only small PPE. Reported post-tax EBIT and rising sales produce superficially attractive return ratios.

Counterevidence: RHP note 50 discloses that certain party balances recorded as trade payables represent cash receipts/payments without underlying purchases/sales or detailed supporting records. Their amount is unknown, and their operating-versus-financing classification is unresolved. Security-deposit recoverability and noncash accretion/amortization complicate the denominator and cash investment bridge. No project/cohort cash return is disclosed.

Judgment: Present exact asset/funding and incremental-capital diagnostics but no reliable sustainable incremental ROIC score. A low fixed-asset base does not prove capital-light economics. [E02, E05, E07, E08] No historical factor above 8: relevant restated history is four years or confidence is Medium; older AS history is qualified rather than discarded.

### CASH: 3 · Medium

FY24–26 reported CFO totals 0.3020 cr against 8.7450 cr group PAT, a 3.45% ratio of sums. CFO is negative in both FY25 and FY26; retentions/security deposits and the wage-liability unwind absorb funds.

Counterevidence: FY24 CFO 3.3509 cr was positive; latest billed receivables declined and IPO capital can fund timing gaps. Reported cash-flow classification has limitations, but plausible corrections do not establish robust customer cash realization.

Judgment: Recurring weak realization, not capex, supports 3. Apply the disclosed GQS≤5 override while retaining NS for missing growth/capital factors; this does not diagnose an actual default. [E02, E07, E08] No historical factor above 8: relevant restated history is four years or confidence is Medium; older AS history is qualified rather than discarded.

### BAL: NS · Low

Mar 31 cash 0.3475 cr is mostly physical cash; pledged deposits are not spendable cash. Debt 7.1797 cr includes on-demand OD 4.0769 cr; the IPO proposes 6.6 cr repayment plus 8 cr working capital.

Counterevidence: Fresh-issue gross 20.66544 cr is meaningful; lenders existed and no lender default was reported. The June debt update and restricted IPO objects are evidence against assuming the issuer has no financing options.

Judgment: Cutoff free cash, actual proceeds deployment, drawing-power availability and maturity conflicts are unresolved. Model shortfalls are conditional experiments, not proof the issuer failed G3. [E02, E08, E12, E14] No historical factor above 8: relevant restated history is four years or confidence is Medium; older AS history is qualified rather than discarded.

### EXEC: 5 · Medium

Revenue and number of projects scaled strongly before FY26, with repeat execution and entry into additional states. The issuer completed the IPO and had an identifiable order base.

Counterevidence: FY26 project count/plant count are flat; concentration in one customer increases, and deductions and recoveries rise to 0.1294 cr. Prospectus quantity/percentage/classification inconsistencies reduce confidence in performance communication.

Judgment: Mixed observable delivery merits 5. There is no invented promise that management never made; post-IPO use-of-proceeds delivery is too recent to judge. [E09, E10, E11, E12] No historical factor above 8: relevant restated history is four years or confidence is Medium; older AS history is qualified rather than discarded.

### EARN: 6 · Medium

Operating EBITDA excluding other income rises 2.9262→5.1393→6.5138 cr across FY24–26, while reported diluted EPS rises 2.36→5.40→7.29. The per-share improvement remains after recalculation using the current share count. Most FY26 PAT originates in operations.

Counterevidence: FY26 margin 7.65% slips from 7.84%; other income 0.5284 cr includes 0.1200 cr write-off income and deposit accretion. FY23–24 and earlier earnings require major AS/Ind AS and direct-reserve restatements.

Judgment: Adequate recurring profit progress with meaningful normalization and per-share caveats. Cash weakness is assessed in CASH, not used as a duplicate arbitrary deduction here. [E01, E02, E07, E12] No historical factor above 8: relevant restated history is four years or confidence is Medium; older AS history is qualified rather than discarded.

### R: NS · Low

The conditional monthly model links growth, collection timing, statutory claims, deposits, capex, financing and whole-share dilution over five/ten years, with 12/15/18% hurdles.

Counterevidence: Optimistic financed operating paths may support returns, but no supported actual entry balance or approved future capital is established.

Judgment: No defensible supported base IRR exists while G2/G3 are unresolved. Conditional stress arithmetic cannot be converted to a numerical return-spread factor. [E14] No historical factor above 8: relevant restated history is four years or confidence is Medium; older AS history is qualified rather than discarded.

### D: NS · Low

The dominant-customer loss/delay path simultaneously cuts revenue, pressures payroll margin and traps unbilled/security claims. Intraperiod and terminal-reserve failures suppress all ordinary shareholder returns.

Counterevidence: New IPO capital and continuing plant operations provide possible buffers; customer public-sector identity does not mean all claims are lost. No quantified liquidation-recovery waterfall is established.

Judgment: Permanent-loss risk is high qualitatively; current shareholder recoveries and credible stress-funding availability are insufficiently evidenced for a numeric factor. [E08, E09, E14] No historical factor above 8: relevant restated history is four years or confidence is Medium; older AS history is qualified rather than discarded.

### P: NS · Low

At the stated 19 October secondary close, current-share PE and enterprise operating-profit cross-checks are demanding for a 7.65% EBITDA-margin, customer-concentrated business. Reverse trials require both earning power and financeability.

Counterevidence: Continued service expansion and actual debt repayment could improve earnings; near-term share-price movements alone do not settle value.

Judgment: Price-implied growth/margins remain assumption-dependent on unverified cash and capital classifications. Retain all trial outcomes without forcing a price-expectations score. [E12, E14, E15] No historical factor above 8: relevant restated history is four years or confidence is Medium; older AS history is qualified rather than discarded.

### L: NS · Low

Listed 5 October 2026, only 11 possible sessions exist through 19 October; 20/60-session histories cannot exist. The 1200-share market lot is supported by a qualified reproduction of the listing notice, making the ₹5 lakh reference position granular.

Counterevidence: Secondary sources corroborate active trading and the 19 October close/volume; the reproduced listing notice and observed trading support the existence of a market. The final listing particulars were not directly verified from the exchange original. Absence of 60 sessions is not zero turnover.

Judgment: Primary traded-value history, stable executable depth/spread and cutoff surveillance verification are insufficient. Price × volume is not exchange turnover; no fabricated 5% exit-days score. [E12, E15] No historical factor above 8: relevant restated history is four years or confidence is Medium; older AS history is qualified rather than discarded.



The only numeric override is the disclosed GQS cap of 5 for CASH = 3 and recurring poor realization. It does not convert an NS aggregate into 5. GOV = 4 does not trigger the severe governance override; no actual unfinanceable default is established, so no funding-failure cap is asserted. G2/G3 holds independently preclude a favorable investment classification. The full matrix cannot assign a numeric cell when its required aggregates are NS. sections.title: Business Overview
sections.content_markdown:
The company maintains electrical, control-and-instrumentation and mechanical systems; operates boiler/turbine/generator, coal-handling and merry-go-round infrastructure; and supplies housekeeping, overhaul and manpower services. Its customer purchases availability, safe staffing, maintenance execution and compliance rather than a proprietary manufactured product. The supplier must recruit and deploy people, fund wages/statutory benefits, provide tender/performance security, execute work and obtain customer certification before invoices and collections. [E09; RHP pp190–219,307–309]

Contracts include annual maintenance engagements commonly lasting one to three years, performance-linked work, manpower supply and short-term bill-of-quantity tasks. The issuer describes a monthly billing process with administrative verification before accounts clearance and approximately 50–60 days for realization. Meanwhile wages are generally due in the first week and statutory payments in the next month. Even a profitable contract can therefore need cash before the customer pays. RHP's historical debtor-day average does not include every retention or security deposit, so it understates the full capital tied to winning and servicing a contract. [E08–E09; RHP pp120–124]

Reported operations cover 21 locations in nine states over the recent three-year window, with electrical licenses in five states at the RHP date. The reported 2,058 personnel is not an annual person-day measure. RHP p195 defines deployed manpower during the year, whereas p199 describes the same figure as at 31 March 2026; neither average annual staffing nor billed hours is established. Another narrative uses 1,969 personnel at a different reporting date. No reconciliation of these definitions or dates is invented. Public-sector revenue is 92.27% in FY26. Government-related customers can reduce some counterparty credit risk while increasing administrative, certification and payment-timing risk. A famous plant or customer is not an endorsement of the security. [E09]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.content_markdown:
Proposed mechanism: tender prequalification, field experience, licenses and local labour organization allow participation in repeat maintenance work. Evidence: repeated contracts and operations across several large power stations. Durability: established staffing, safety routines and proven execution take time to replicate. Failure mode: a capable competing contractor can recruit similar personnel, meet qualification requirements and underbid; a customer can rebid or reduce scope. The record does not quantify switching costs, sustained pricing power or a defined market-share denominator. [E09–E10]

Concentration has worsened: the largest customer's share rises from 49.99% in FY24 to 74.77% in FY26. Losing one award, delayed certification or an unrecovered wage increase can overwhelm the benefit from many smaller client logos. Repeat business supports operational credibility, but concentration and repeated public tenders make it a mixed rather than strong moat. The document's repeat-revenue table is not internally additive: its FY26 repeat amount plus new-customer revenue exceeds total revenue. The narrative 99.65% figure is attributed to management, not treated as a precisely reconciled audited KPI. [E09–E11]

The following named peers are economic comparators, not exchange-sector lookalikes. Lakshya Powertech supplies a relevant but financially weaker power/industrial services comparator. Power Mech is a much larger diversified engineering and O&M contractor, providing scale/context but not a directly transferable margin or multiple. Neptunus is a higher-value technical/OEM-linked maintenance benchmark, not an exact manpower outsourcing peer. Differences in perimeter, dates and rating versus audit evidence are explicit. Reported expansion is not automatically real volume. Neither acquired subsidiaries nor currency translation explains the sales increase: the issuer has no line-by-line subsidiaries and transactions are described as INR-only. However, service scope, tariff recovery, minimum-wage escalation, person-days and contract mix are not separately quantified. FY26 reports the same 15 plants and 36 projects as FY25, with a lower reported personnel count. That does not prove shrinking activity: the document mixes during-year and March 31 descriptions, and neither is a measure of annual person-days supplied. It does mean gross sales alone cannot establish volume growth. [E09–E11]

A useful economic cross-check is revenue less employee expense, explicitly **not gross profit** because it still excludes consumables and other delivery costs. It grows more slowly than gross sales in the recent window. The still narrower revenue less payroll and materials is ₹1.5000/5.9583/7.1949/8.5221 crore in FY23/24/25/26; its FY24–26 CAGR is 19.595%. This is another service residual, not an accounting gross-margin reconstruction. The exceptionally thin FY23 residual is a distorted earnings base, so the larger three-year percentage cannot be treated as stable repeatable economics. Without a bounded price/scope/pass-through bridge, REV remains NS. The numerical schedule's ≥30% starting score of 9 and history ceiling of 8 are disclosed diagnostics, not assigned scores. sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.content_markdown:
The installed coal-power base requires maintenance even without rapid capacity additions, but Sai Urja accesses that demand only through awards, renewals, staffing and cash. The 15 June gross contract value of ₹159.6704 crore includes ₹62.6520 crore already invoiced. The unexecuted ₹97.0184 crore comprises ₹71.6510 crore on ongoing projects plus ₹25.3674 crore yet to commence. It is about one year's current revenue, spread over contract terms and subject to execution, not a five-year revenue guarantee. No fully reconciled October backlog roll-forward, cancellation schedule or guaranteed margin was found. [E10]

A cutoff-era update must be kept separate: dated 18 October secondary filing metadata and corroborating news report L1 (lowest-bidder) status for a ₹12.98 crore NTECL C&I repair/rectification engagement, described as approximately three years plus one day and five unit overhauls. The underlying BSE filing was inaccessible, and no firm award or start/end dates were established. This is a positive conditional pipeline observation, not executed backlog; neither the June unexecuted total nor model sales is increased by ₹12.98 crore. Conversion and working-capital terms require monitoring. [E10; dated secondary sources in source map]

Growth is not mainly a factory-capex story. Deposits, retention, unbilled work, wage timing and performance guarantees require capital. Contract security is paid at commencement and may remain tied up for six months to three years; the note explicitly leaves some release dates undefined. The company cannot use the same deposit simultaneously as productive contract capital, free debt-netting cash and a terminal distribution. Our capital diagnostic includes it, and the cash model funds increases. [E08]

Definition: operating assets less non-interest operating liabilities, excluding cash, investments and income-tax/deferred-tax assets; pledged contract FD remains productive committed capital. Financing-side reconciliation adds equity,debt,leases and net tax liability, less those nonoperating assets. Detailed component values are in financial_inputs.json/metrics.json.


These returns are accounting diagnostics, not sustainable project IRRs. The unsupported trade-payable fund movements may be financing rather than operating supplier credit; classifying them incorrectly changes both cash conversion and invested capital. Deposit amortization/accretion, leases, tax assets, asset additions and original/restated vintages also matter. The net-investment reconciliation therefore displays its residual rather than fabricating a closed three/five-year cash-return bridge. CAP stays NS even when the arithmetic produces attractive apparent returns. Five-year incremental ROIC is NS because a comparable opening invested-capital and normalized earnings series is not established. [E01,E05,E07–E08]

Bottom-up scenarios are conditional operating programs. At the starting margin, payroll and other direct costs consume most sales, so even moderate growth requires explicit funding of collections and contract deposits. The model links annualized revenue to monthly operating cash, margin, receivable days, security/retention requirements, capital additions and financing. The terminal reinvestment requirement derives from the return actually earned on modeled capital, capped by the scenario target, rather than assuming a flattering ROIC indefinitely. Required operating-cash growth is another investment because that cash is not in productive IC. [E14]

Harsh Ajaykumar Mittal and Santosh Ajay Kumar Mittal are the promoter directors. Stewardship is judged from the original record, not promoter ownership alone. Original FY21–23 CARO reports exclude PF and ESI from the assertion that no undisputed statutory dues were over six months old. Later records offer counterevidence: the ₹7.31 lakh IGST liability for FY2021–22, due 31 December 2022, was paid 26 August 2025, and FY26 CARO reports no such long-overdue undisputed dues. It is misleading to call the settled amount a current default. An OCR artifact initially resembling ₹27.31 lakh was resolved against the image; it is not an issuer inconsistency. [E03–E04]

The audit-trail chronology is more serious than a generic clean-audit label. FY24 explicitly reports an ineffective feature and inability to verify integrity. FY25's main-report double negative is ambiguous, but its own note 53 explicitly states the trail was not maintained. FY26 says the software has the feature without enough specific evidence of uninterrupted operation, no tampering and preservation to close the earlier finding. Main and IFC opinions remain unmodified. Both statements are retained. [E03]

FY25 note 52 and the later RHP note 50 disclose some trade-payable balances without underlying purchases/sales or detailed supporting records, representing fund receipts/payments classified on management representations. Their amount and counterparties are ND. This does not mean every payable is unsupported, nor does it prove money was diverted; it does prevent a reliable cash/capital assessment. FY26 original statements omit that paragraph while the later IPO RHP retains it. Omission is not affirmative remediation. [E05]

Related-party exposure needs gross-flow analysis. FY26 promoter loans of ₹2.735 crore were both received and repaid; Shikhar expenses reimbursed by Sai Urja were ₹1.5026 crore. The ₹0.4999 crore property advance to a promoter was recovered in FY25. Promoter/director remuneration is meaningful but not the entire RPT picture; a small expense-summary percentage omits financing and reimbursements. End-year RPT totals combine different assets and liabilities, so they are not a net exposure. Ownership in partnership associates, premises leases and related suppliers should be monitored contract by contract. [E06]

### Sai Urja monthly cash, claims and conditional-return specification

#### Scope and reproducibility

model.py uses only the Python standard library and reads only adjacent model_inputs.json unless an input mapping is supplied. It never reads a source PDF, network endpoint, another issuer's files or a third-party package. API: run(M, label, scenario, years, overrides=None, **changes); build_models(M=None, destination=None). Monetary arithmetic uses Decimal with 60-digit intermediate precision and 1e-18-crore ledger rounding. Shares are integers. Monetary outputs are lossless strings. JSON serialization is canonical and gzip timestamps are zero; all 687 full paths, including failures, are retained. The independent verify_model.py does not import the engine or trust self-certified reconciliation flags. It independently reconstructs the current and noncurrent gratuity schedules and rejects both missing-payment and duplicate-payment mutations.

These are conditional experiments, not forecasts or a reconstruction of actual cash balances. The 31 March 2026 opening precedes the 19 October 2026 secondary-market entry. Seven explicitly unobserved bridge periods and exactly 60 or 120 post-entry monthly periods are retained. Actual June borrowing differs from March; the model does not claim that later bank balances, proceeds deployment or drawing power are known. A hypothetical funding failure is not an actual default. No supported base IRR follows from a merely hypothetical financing rescue.

#### Operating capital and earnings

Opening reported cash 0.3475 includes bank 0.0068 and physical cash 0.3407; a bank-balance-only sensitivity is separate. No unused sanction becomes cash automatically. Gross AR 10.515 includes 0.3713 doubtful, older-than-two-year balances without an allowance. That amount remains permanently locked in modeled AR, generates no collections or terminal recovery and still burdens productive capital. The remaining good AR follows the scenario DSO. Other working-capital stocks are inventory, other operating financial assets, contract deposits/EMD/retentions, payables and customer advances; ratios move linearly from opening to target over the first year while revenue compounds by actual days/365. All positive working-capital changes are funded at period start and releases arrive only at the ending 19th.

Contract deposits, EMD and retentions 9.1135 plus pledged FD 0.4502 are not free cash. Their full amounts enter productive capital. The pledged FD remains unavailable; contract capital moves with its modeled revenue ratio. Other current financial assets 1.0326 include prepaid expenses and unquantified prepaid IPO costs and are not independently monetized. No refund of the income-tax asset 0.2209 is assumed. Listed investments 0.1636 and equity-accounted associate investment 0.2075 are nonoperating, added separately at book value only when the survival tests permit valuation. This is not an associate fair-value estimate. Associate PAT 0.0444 is not consolidated revenue or recurring parent cash generation. There is no subsidiary, minority-interest deduction or invented NCI.

Operating EBITDA equals run-rate-derived period revenue times the scenario margin. Physical PPE/ROU/intangible depreciation uses annual 0.4719 divided by opening assets 1.7782, applied to opening carrying assets plus the month's cash capex. Security-deposit amortization 0.2945 and EIR income 0.2965 are both excluded from this forward cash/earnings convention; the underlying full deposits remain productive capital. Historical reported total D&A 0.7664 and EBIT 5.7474 are unchanged in historical reporting. Cash capex is max(0.9% of revenue, 0.7584 annual maintenance floor), prorated by days. This is an assumption, not a commitment forecast. PPE rolls by additions less physical depreciation.

#### Claims and event ordering

Opening statutory claims 2.0242 and other cash claims 1.1203 (including audit fee) settle over 12 assumed installments. They are not included again in recurring trade payables. Opening gratuity 0.8334 comprises current 0.7376 and noncurrent 0.0958. The current portion is settled across the first 12 assumed monthly start installments; the noncurrent portion is settled across the subsequent 48. Each installment is bounded by its remaining component, with the final installment settling rounding residue. Every payment reduces free cash and the aggregate liability once, so only the remaining provision reduces productive invested capital. The separately labeled full-payment stress on 19 March 2027 accelerates only the then-remaining provision, allocating payment to current before noncurrent and never repaying an amount already settled. No opening gratuity remains at the 5- or 10-year terminal dates. These are conservative analyst timing assumptions, not assertions about actual due dates, payments or default. Future payroll cash costs remain in the operating-cost assumptions; no new unpaid gratuity provision or additional cash tax benefit is created. The prior FY25 IGST 7.31 lakh was settled on 26 August 2025, before the opening, and is never paid twice. There is no opening income-tax liability; the net tax asset is not cash. Opening interest is set to 0 because a separately quantified accrued-interest payable was not disclosed in the supplied mapping, not as a claim that no accrual existed.

Each period processes dated financing/IPO events at the starting boundary (April 1 for the first period after the March 31 closing balance), then opening claims, scheduled opening-gratuity installments, scheduled principal, positive working-capital investment and capex. A specified portion of cash operating costs is paid seven days later, before collections. Named events between boundaries occur on their exact dates, never accelerated. Cash interest is the integral of outstanding debt times its applicable annual rate times exact days/365 between principal events; it is paid at the ending boundary before collections. The first day between the March 31 closing balance and April 1 payments accrues on opening debt, then dated principal changes determine subsequent daily interest. Ending collections equal revenue less the remaining operating costs. Negative working-capital release then arrives. Taxes accrue at the disclosed 25.168% section 115BAA rate on positive EBIT less actual modeled cash interest, without a loss-tax cash benefit; accumulated tax is paid at ending 19ths in March, June, September and December. Legacy tax/interest claims remain distinct from current accruals.

Financial debt is tracked separately for term loans 2.4020, dropline 0.6987, OD 4.0769, card 0.0021, lease 0.1044 and new hypothetical bank principal. The first 12 term installments cover 1.1324, the remaining 1.2696 amortizes over 36 installments. Dropline amortizes over 60 installments; a conflicting 12-month tenor is tested by an accelerated March 2027 maturity. Leases amortize over 60 installments and the card settles initially. OD either matures at assumed 19 March 2027 or is conditionally renewed at the same cap; renewal creates no new cash and renewed principal remains a next-year terminal obligation. Interest assumptions are disclosed rather than presented as verified future offers.

#### IPO and conditional financing

Pre-IPO 5,810,000 shares increase by 1,828,800 fresh shares at ₹113 on assumed 5 October 2026 proceeds availability; gross issuer proceeds 20.66544 are exact. The 379,200 OFS shares and earlier secondary transactions contribute no company cash. The issuer's fresh cash is divided into restricted WC 8, restricted debt-repayment 6.6, assumed remaining IPO fees 1, and residual general cash. Remaining fees are incremental unpaid fees only, not prepaid fees counted again; their amount is unobserved, so zero/two-crore sensitivities are retained. Restricted WC may pay only positive productive WC investment and precollection operating payments. Restricted debt cash repays card, OD, dropline and term principal on assumed 19 October 2026. Unspent earmarked balances remain restricted and are excluded from terminal excess cash; no automatic reallocation or current actual utilization is asserted.

Default new financing is absent. A separately hypothetical future-funded case draws capped 10 crore on 19 November 2026 (1% fee, 12% interest, 12-month grace and 36-installment repayment) and places up to 20 crore gross equity on 19 December 2026 at 75% of the trial's entry price (2% fee). Equity shares = min(floor(gross target / issue price), 2 million shares, authorization headroom). Verified authorization 11 million is binding; 14 million expanded authorization is a separately hypothetical dated approval and never silently assumed. Future debt/equity draw windows are explicitly bounded. No unsupported finance is treated as an issuer commitment.

The separately hypothetical early 5 funded case shifts the same bank instrument to 1 April 2026 and reduces its gross amount to 5 crore. It is a counterfactual bridge experiment, not an April financing assertion. Early 0.9231 mathematical unused-sanction, 3 crore and 10 crore cases are separate. The 0.9231 upper bound has no verified drawing-power availability and June debt indicates much smaller contemporaneous headroom. All unfinanced and future-only paths retain earlier shortfalls even after later money arrives.

#### Survival, reinvestment and valuation

Every event records exact pool changes, claim changes, free-cash change and date/share state; running free cash and all restricted/claim balances are losslessly reconstructed from opening. Monthly opening/closing pool and claim checkpoints, cash minima and the first breach provide independent cross-checks. Each full event is stored once globally and monthly rows carry its exact sequence references. Every event updates free cash, all restricted pools and every claim exactly. Restricted pools and claims may never become negative. Any free-cash value below zero permanently blocks all ordinary terminal EV, shareholder value, IRR/CAGR, hurdle price and normalized P/E return. The negative number is a hypothetical unfunded diagnostic balance, not an overdraft. Later proceeds cannot cure an earlier missed obligation. All subsequent diagnostic events and every failed trial remain visible.

A cash-surviving path must also cover its terminal reserve: one next-year operating month plus all unpaid income taxes, one month cash interest and next 12-month principal. A renewed OD is entirely reserved as a next-year maturity, not forgiven or indefinitely refinanced. Reserve failure suppresses ordinary returns. Every WACC/g sensitivity cell independently recomputes its reserve and sustainability gate.

Productive invested capital = closing ONWC net of any remaining opening gratuity + PPE/ROU/intangibles + capital advance + pledged deposits. ONWC includes the full contract deposits/EMD/retentions and permanently uncollected doubtful invoices. Neither operating cash nor nonoperating investments are in this denominator. Earned ROIC = min(scenario target, positive normalized NOPAT / actual modeled productive IC). Next-year NOPAT grows by g; productive reinvestment = next-year NOPAT × g / earned ROIC. Required operating cash also grows from one current month of cash operating costs to one next-year month; its positive increase is additionally deducted because operating cash is excluded from productive IC. Terminal FCFF = next-year NOPAT − productive reinvestment − operating cash growth. Positive NOPAT, ROIC > g, WACC > g and positive FCFF are all required.

Operating EV = FCFF / (WACC − g). Ordinary equity = EV + cash above operating/tax/interest reserves + separate nonoperating investments − all financial debt/leases − unpaid legacy non-tax claims, floored at zero. The full principal-inclusive reserve remains a funding gate, not a second subtraction of debt principal. Unspent IPO cash and pledged FD are not added as distributable cash. No free-cash subtotal is discounted and also counted in terminal retained cash. No post-entry dividends are assumed. Shareholder terminal price uses the actual terminal integer share count, including future dilution; CAGR uses exactly 5 or 10 entry-to-exit anniversary years.

Normalized P/E cross-checks use next-year parent EBIT less financing interest and tax, then add excess cash and separate nonoperating investments. Debt is not subtracted again from P/E equity value. The 10/15/20 multiples are transparent illustrative checks, not verified peer fair values or a substitute for the operating EV model. All P/E outputs obey the same survival gates.

#### Search design and outputs

Core bear/base/bull cases span both 5/10-year horizons and unfinanced, future-funded and early 5 funded policies. Operating two-way sensitivity is 4 growth rates × 4 margins × 2 horizons. Each full path contains 3 WACCs × 3 terminal-growth cells. Reverse growth tests 0–100% inclusive in 5-percentage-point increments for both horizons and all three financing policies, retaining all failures and reporting sampled growth satisfying 1×/5×/10× and 12%/15%/18% hurdles. No monotonicity or solution outside this finite grid is claimed.

Entry-price re-solving runs all three operating scenarios and both horizons at every price ₹1, 6, ..., 401. Every path recalculates the future equity price at 75% of entry, integer shares, legal headroom, actual proceeds/fees, monthly cash and terminal reserve. The highest sampled price satisfying each 12%/15%/18% hurdle is reported, not a continuous root or purchase recommendation. The algebraic terminal price / (1 + hurdle)^years figure separately holds simulated financing terms fixed and must not be substituted for the fully repriced search. Failed low-price paths are retained; a cheaper share price is not assumed to preserve funding proceeds.

model_summary.json is the compact reader; canonical_paths.json.gz contains all 687 complete paths in a streamable JSON array, one path per line. trial_index.csv covers every trial and annual_model.csv contains all forecast-year rollforwards for 18 core paths. Model-derived values must be regenerated together after input changes. Neither an attractive hypothetical path nor a successful numerical verification resolves the audited financing-like trade-payable support gap or makes the base assumptions investable.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.content_markdown:
The strongest bear case is a loss or delayed renewal of the largest customer, or slower certification of its unbilled work. Revenue falls while labour, statutory payments and site costs cannot instantly adjust. Margins compress; security deposits and retention are released late; a performance guarantee or labour claim consumes more cash. Borrowing access then depends on drawing power, collateral, timely compliance and lenders. Rescue equity, if available, may dilute current holders at an unfavorable price. This is a linked business/cash/financing path, not a standalone P/E derating. [E04–E10,E14]

The single thesis-break variable is **cash-backed validity and collection of recognized service claims after wages, statutory dues and contract-security funding**. Rising accounting sales are not enough. Evidence that the disputed classification is merely ordinary, fully documented financing and that earned claims collect would materially improve the thesis. Conversely, substantiated material uncollectible revenue or abusive fund use is more serious than a temporary share-price decline. [E05,E08]

Permanent-loss risk is assessed qualitatively as High, with confidence constrained by the missing liability/recovery detail. This does not mean a default has occurred or is forecast with a stated probability. Main audits are unmodified, old IGST was settled, promoter loans were repaid, IPO cash was raised and real work continues. Those are the strongest counterarguments to an overly severe reading. They do not independently close accounting support or establish funded growth. No exact liquidation recovery is asserted. [E03–E06,E12]

The market may already price growth and the new IPO float; no claim of informational uniqueness is made. What differentiates this analysis is the separation of gross contract value from unexecuted work, operating cash from accounting profit, legal capital issuance from hypothetical finance and observed financial concerns from unsupported accusations.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.content_markdown:
A fivefold share-price return needs about 37.97% annual growth over five years or 17.46% over ten; tenfold requires about 58.49% or 25.89%. Business sales growth, enterprise-value growth and per-share return are not interchangeable. With positive consistent earnings, price multiple equals revenue multiple × net-margin ratio × initial/final diluted shares × terminal/entry P/E. In this issuer, new-share funding and working-capital needs must be solved with that identity, not added afterward. [E14]

The engine retains 687 full paths; 310 have ordinary returns suppressed. Reverse-growth and entry-financing details above specify each tested horizon, funding policy and admissibility rule. No failed path is presented as an ordinary return.

Outcome classification: **Speculative / unsupported**, not an asserted impossibility. A much stronger operating outcome would need retained contract economics, collection and capital access beyond what is currently verified. Nominal sales compounding alone would not suffice if wage pass-through absorbs most revenue, deposits consume funds or repeated low-price issuance dilutes shareholders. The finite model grid is a disclosed experiment, not a universal proof that no imaginable fivefold or tenfold outcome can exist.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.content_markdown:
**Hold — unresolved; pending evidence.** No BQS/GQS/IAS point score is assigned, and the company should not be placed at the bottom of ranked businesses as though missingness proved weak quality. GOV, MOAT, DUR, CASH, EXEC and EARN judgments are visible, but the unresolved growth/capital/funding factors keep the aggregates incomplete. G2 excludes a favorable investment classification; G3 is a hold, not an evidenced failure. G4 is conditional for a new and granular SME market. [E01–E15]

It does not meet the compounder requirements: no established strong moat, reliable incremental-return factor, adequate demonstrated cash conversion or resolved critical gates. A lower quoted price alone cannot cure unverified liabilities or cash. After documentary closure, current bank/debt/proceeds reconciliation and a credible service-volume/collection bridge, rebuild the entire analysis, including any changed price, shares and liquidity. Only then apply the numerical matrix. For an existing holder, the appropriate research action is to review reliability, funding and exit constraints before making a portfolio decision; position weights, taxes and objectives were not supplied, so no trade or allocation instruction is invented.
